lessons.title: Claim checking
lessons.subtitle: Week 7: Verification and information literacy
lessons.body:
Break an answer into checkable claims. Verify important claims against appropriate original evidence rather than judging only tone or length.

Offline practice: Underline factual claims in a fictional school announcement and list evidence needed for each. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Break an answer into checkable claims. Verify important claims against appropriate original evidence rather than judging only tone or length.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
lessons.sourceName: UNESCO guidance on responsible AI in education

options: Every task requires training a new model.
Break an answer into checkable claims. Verify important claims against appropriate original evidence rather than judging only tone or length.
A polished AI answer is enough evidence that every claim is correct.
The human learner never needs to check the result.
questions.explanation: Break an answer into checkable claims. Verify important claims against appropriate original evidence rather than judging only tone or length.

questions.prompt: For the activity “Underline factual claims in a fictional school announcement and list evidence needed for each.”, which approach demonstrates learning?
options: Skip the activity and copy an unrelated answer.
Complete the activity, explain your reasoning, and record a limitation.
Share someone else’s private information to make the example realistic.
Treat an unverified generated response as final evidence.
questions.explanation: The activity asks you to apply this lesson. A written explanation and limitation make your understanding reviewable; a copied result alone does not.

questions.prompt: You return to the “Claim checking” lesson after a break without internet. What can you do next?
options: Delete your previous work and start the whole course again.
Recall the key idea, check saved notes, and complete the offline activity.
Assume a cloud assistant will respond without a connection.
Wait until you can buy a paid AI subscription.
questions.explanation: The lesson and practice do not require an online tool. Retrieval and a small saved activity help you resume.

lessons.title: Source quality
lessons.subtitle: Week 7: Verification and information literacy
lessons.body:
A source should have relevant expertise and evidence for the specific claim. An official page can still be outdated or irrelevant to the question.

lessons.title: Numbers and calculations
lessons.subtitle: Week 7: Verification and information literacy
lessons.body:
Recalculate important numbers independently. Check units, assumptions, and rounding. A correct arithmetic result can still answer the wrong question.

lessons.title: Changing information
lessons.subtitle: Week 7: Verification and information literacy
lessons.body:
Prices, deadlines, rules, and service features can change. Record when information was checked and avoid presenting old details as current.

Offline practice: Design a verification note with source, date, claim, and uncertainty for a fictional application deadline. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Prices, deadlines, rules, and service features can change. Record when information was checked and avoid presenting old details as current.

lessons.title: Uncertainty log
lessons.subtitle: Week 7: Verification and information literacy
lessons.body:
A verification log distinguishes supported, contradicted, and unresolved claims. An unresolved claim should remain uncertain until adequate evidence is found.

Offline practice: Build a three-row verification log and decide which claims belong in a final resource. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A verification log distinguishes supported, contradicted, and unresolved claims. An unresolved claim should remain uncertain until adequate evidence is found.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
